method: Sector score = average five-pillar composite of the book's names in that sector. Trend reflects the Aug 19 session and the current macro regime.

sectors.name: Energy
sectors.note: Only major sector higher on Aug 19 (+1.8%). Hormuz stays closed, Brent settled around $91-93.

sectors.name: Financials
sectors.note: Steeper long end helps net interest income but hurts deal flow; JPM still near its 52-week high.

sectors.name: Consumer / LatAm
sectors.note: MercadoLibre +7.3% and Nu +1.8% against a falling index.

sectors.name: Healthcare
sectors.note: Clear defensive rotation — Lilly +4.5%, Boston Scientific +3.1%, Intuitive +1.7% on a red day.

sectors.name: Cybersecurity
sectors.note: Defensive spending, offensive multiple — sold off with high-growth software.

sectors.name: Software / AI
sectors.note: Mixed: ServiceNow +6.5% and Alphabet green, but high-multiple software is exposed to the yield move.

sectors.name: Semiconductors
sectors.note: PHLX Semi Index fell ~5.6% with all 30 components lower — the epicentre of the selloff.

sectors.name: AI infrastructure
sectors.note: Broadcom -4.6%, Seagate -7.9%, Arista -3.5%. Structural demand intact, tape is not.

sectors.name: AI power / nuclear
sectors.note: Power names outperformed a falling tape; data-centre demand is unaffected by the rate move.

sectors.name: Industrials
sectors.note: Sector fell ~1.5%; GE Aerospace -5.0% as higher oil raises airline costs.

sectors.name: Renewables
sectors.note: Higher fossil prices modestly improve the relative case, but the group is rate-sensitive.

sectors.name: Uranium & nuclear fuel
sectors.note: Energy-security bid plus long-term uranium contracting near multi-year highs.
